entry.title: Embedding (#29, Dart): runtime knobs, VAD sensitivity, resetSession, …
entry.content:
<pre style='white-space:pre-wrap;width:81ex'>Embedding (#29, Dart): runtime knobs, VAD sensitivity, resetSession, audio_s/switched/model_load events (#42)
* chore: sync mobile/ lockfile with hayamimi_core's declared deps
mobile/pubspec.lock hadn't been regenerated since hayamimi_core's pubspec.yaml picked up its archive/posix transitive dependencies, so `flutter pub get`/`flutter analyze` in mobile/ was resolving them fresh every run instead of reading a pinned version. Running the verification gate for this change surfaced the drift; syncing it now keeps the demo app's resolved dependency set reproducible.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* routing: thread decodingMethod/hotwords/onModelLoad into RoutedRecognizerSet.build, add reset()
RoutedRecognizerSet.build hardcoded 'modified_beam_search' for the ja tier with no way to override it, never exposed sherpa-onnx's hotwords feature, and had no way to observe when each of its three model builds started/finished. It also had no way to clear currentLang for a fresh "conversation" without freeing and rebuilding all three native models.
Add decodingMethod (default unchanged: 'modified_beam_search' for ja), hotwordsFile/hotwordsScore (both applied only to the ja tier -- the routed profile's only tier that runs a plain transducer decode), and an optional onModelLoad('ja'|'sensevoice'|'lid', 'start'|'done', ms) callback fired around each background-isolate build. Kept as a plain callback rather than a dependency on any event type, so this file stays free of anything beyond sherpa-onnx and its own model-resolving helpers; LiveTranscriber is what turns the callback into its own ModelLoadEvent stream.
Add reset(), which just clears currentLang: RoutedRecognizerSet never populates resolveStickyLang's pending/count state (see that function's doc -- it has no production callers on mobile today), so there's nothing else session-scoped to clear.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* live: pure-Dart pieces for VAD sensitivity, model-load events, mutable refine cap
LiveTranscriptEntry had no way to carry a segment's audio duration or whether it caused a routed session's language to switch, so neither could reach a UI or the wire event types. Add audioSeconds (nullable -- drafts never measure it) and switched (default false).
Add VadSensitivity, an immutable value class for Silero VAD's four tunable knobs (threshold, min-silence/min-speech/max-speech durations), defaulting to sherpa-onnx's own values so VadSensitivity() reproduces today's unconfigurable behavior exactly; validated in its constructor (threshold in (0, 1], durations positive/finite) since a bad value here would otherwise silently mistune segmentation. Alongside it, shouldSwapVadNow(speechActive, busy) is the pure "is it safe to swap in a rebuilt VAD right now" decision (never mid-segment, never while a decode is in flight) -- pulled out as its own testable function the same way isDraftDue/isAutoRefineDue already are, since the actual swap needs FFI and can't be unit tested directly.
Add ModelLoadEvent, the plain data LiveTranscriber.modelLoads will emit around each native model's background-isolate build.
RefineBuffer.maxDurationSeconds becomes a mutable field instead of final, so LiveTranscriber's refineBufferMaxSeconds runtime setter can change the cap without rebuilding the buffer or touching any native model.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* live: runtime pacing knobs, decodingMethod/VAD sensitivity/hotwords, resetSession, model-load events
LiveTranscriber's pacing (draft interval/window/min-audio, auto-refine silence/max-buffered, refine buffer cap), decoding method, and VAD sensitivity were all frozen constants or sherpa-onnx defaults baked in at _buildNativeState time, with no way for an embedding app to tune any of them for its own device/environment. There was also no way to start a fresh "conversation" without paying to reload up to 396 MB of models, and start()/startDebugWavStream() were one opaque Future with no visibility into which of up to three models was currently loading.
Pacing knobs: draftIntervalSeconds/draftWindowSeconds/ minDraftAudioSeconds/autoRefineSilenceSeconds/ autoRefineMaxBufferedSeconds/refineBufferMaxSeconds are now constructor parameters AND same-named runtime-settable properties, validated (positive, finite) with ArgumentError. Validation runs before the constructor defaults `recorder` to a fresh AudioRecorder() (Dart evaluates an initializer list left to right) -- AudioRecorder()'s own constructor kicks off a real asynchronous platform-channel call under the hood, so an invalid knob value now fails cleanly and synchronously instead of also leaking a half-started platform call.
decodingMethod: start()/startDebugWavStream() gained a decodingMethod parameter (null keeps prior behavior -- 'greedy_search' on the plain path, 'modified_beam_search' on the routed ja tier).
VAD sensitivity: start()/startDebugWavStream() gained a vadSensitivity parameter, and setVadSensitivity() rebuilds Silero VAD off-isolate and swaps it in the moment shouldSwapVadNow says it's safe to (checked once per processed frame via _maybeSwapPendingVad, so no timer polling is needed) -- never mid-segment. Overlapping setVadSensitivity calls collapse to the latest target rather than queueing every one; a stale in-flight build is freed rather than installed. If no session is running, the value is just remembered for the next start().
Hotwords: start()/startDebugWavStream() gained hotwordsFile/ hotwordsScore, applied to the plain path and (via RoutedRecognizerSet's new parameters) the routed ja tier. No runtime setter -- baked into the recognizer at build time.
resetSession(): clears the refine buffer, draft state, and (for a routed session) RoutedRecognizerSet's language lock, without touching any native model. Waits for an in-flight decode to finish first (a 20ms poll of the existing _busy flag, matching stopDebugWavStream's own poll style, rather than a new mutex). No-op, no event, when no session is running.
Model-load events: _buildNativeState now wraps each native build (vad/recognizer, or ja/sensevoice/lid via RoutedRecognizerSet's onModelLoad) with start/done emissions on the new modelLoads stream, including elapsed build time on 'done'. setVadSensitivity's own rebuild emits the same 'vad' events.
Entries: _decodeSegment/_decodeSegmentRouted now populate LiveTranscriptEntry.audioSeconds (segment sample count / 16000) and .switched (from RoutedDecodeResult.switched, previously read and discarded); refineNow() populates audioSeconds with the refined group's total duration.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* embed: surface audioSeconds/switched, model-load, and session-reset events on HayamimiLive
The new LiveTranscriber-level data (LiveTranscriptEntry.audioSeconds/ .switched, modelLoads, sessionResets) had nowhere to go on the wire: FinalSubtitleEvent/RefineSubtitleEvent didn't carry audioSeconds or switched, and there was no event type for model-load progress or a session reset -- so a host app (or SubtitleBroadcastServer's LAN consumers) had no way to see any of it.
FinalSubtitleEvent gains audioSeconds ("audio_s") and switched ("switched"); RefineSubtitleEvent gains audioSeconds only, per the wire design both this and the Python side of issue #29 implement. Add ModelLoadSubtitleEvent ("model_load": model/phase/ms) and SessionResetSubtitleEvent ("session_reset", no payload). All existing keys are unchanged, so this is additive on the wire; the desktop overlay's JS already ignores unrecognized types.
HayamimiLive's constructor now forwards the six pacing knobs to the LiveTranscriber it creates for itself (ignored if a transcriber is injected instead -- configure that one directly), mirrors its runtime setters, forwards decodingMethod/vadSensitivity/hotwordsFile/ hotwordsScore through start()/startDebugWavStream(), adds setVadSensitivity()/resetSession() pass-throughs, and subscribes to the new modelLoads/sessionResets streams to translate them into ModelLoadSubtitleEvent/SessionResetSubtitleEvent on `events` -- the same "LiveTranscriber emits its own domain type, HayamimiLive maps it onto SubtitleEvent" split entries/refineEntries/drafts/errors already use, so LiveTranscriber itself never has to depend on the SubtitleEvent hierarchy.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* server: add bindAddress/allowOrigin to SubtitleBroadcastServer
SubtitleBroadcastServer bound InternetAddress.anyIPv4 and hardcoded Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * unconditionally, with no way for a host app to narrow either -- issue #30's ask, which hadn't landed on the Dart side yet (git log on this file showed nothing past the original extraction).
Add bindAddress (defaults to InternetAddress.anyIPv4, documented as deliberate: LAN reachability from other devices is this class's whole point, so narrowing it to loopback defeats the purpose -- only worth doing if a host app specifically wants same-device-only consumers) and allowOrigin (defaults to '*', matching the desktop subtitle_server.py's permissive default). Existing callers that pass neither keep today's behavior unchanged.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* test: cover the new runtime-config knobs and wire events
Adds coverage for everything in the previous four commits that's reachable without the sherpa-onnx native libs or a real mic:
- subtitle_event_test.dart: fixes the two FinalSubtitleEvent JSON-shape assertions broken by the new audio_s/switched keys, and adds cases for RefineSubtitleEvent's audio_s, ModelLoadSubtitleEvent, and SessionResetSubtitleEvent. - vad_sensitivity_test.dart: VadSensitivity's constructor validation (threshold bounds, positive/finite durations) and all four shouldSwapVadNow truth-table cases. - live_transcriber_config_test.dart: the six pacing knobs' constructor defaults/custom values/validation and runtime-setter validation (installed via the same fake-RecordPlatform approach lifecycle_test.dart uses, since AudioRecorder() touches a platform channel even when nothing else does); resetSession()/setVadSensitivity() as no-ops when no session is running. - hayamimi_live_events_test.dart: a _FakeLiveTranscriber (same pattern hayamimi_live_text_transform_test.dart uses) exercising LiveTranscriptEntry -> FinalSubtitleEvent/RefineSubtitleEvent audioSeconds/switched propagation, modelLoads/sessionResets -> ModelLoadSubtitleEvent/SessionResetSubtitleEvent, resetSession() delegation, and HayamimiLive's constructor/setters forwarding the pacing knobs to its own transcriber.
Not covered here (needs real FFI/model files, same as the rest of RoutedRecognizerSet): RoutedRecognizerSet.reset()'s effect itself -- its bootstrap-after-reset behavior (currentLang/lastLang both null) is already exercised by lang_routing_test.dart's existing null-lastLang resolveDualConfirm cases, since reset() only ever clears that one field.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* docs: document runtime configuration, resetSession, and the full events table
The README's "Recommended configurations" section described the pacing defaults as fixed constructor parameters, and had no mention at all of decodingMethod, VAD sensitivity, hotwords, resetSession(), or the two new event types -- all landed in the preceding commits with no user- facing documentation of how or why to use them.
Add a "Runtime configuration and session control" section: a table of the six pacing knobs (default, runtime-settable, what each does) plus prose on decodingMethod/VAD sensitivity/hotwords/resetSession() that leads with the problem each solves before the API, per this package's usual style. Add an "Events" section: a full JSON-shape table for every SubtitleEvent type this package emits, including why a custom consumer should still switch on `type` defensively (this package's own overlay already does, safely, for the two new types). Touch up the "Broadcasting to other apps on the LAN" section for SubtitleBroadcastServer's new bindAddress/allowOrigin parameters, and the "Package layout" bullets for the two new lib/live/ files and the two new SubtitleEvent subclasses.
CHANGELOG.md: added entries under 0.1.0 (not yet published) for all of the above.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* live: fix native-state leak on partial build failure, lost setVadSensitivity during start(), and a stale-VAD-install race
Review round on the runtime-config work turned up three related bugs in how LiveTranscriber manages native state across start()/stop()/ setVadSensitivity():
1. start()/_runDebugWavStream() awaited _buildNativeState unguarded. If it built the recognizer (or routed set) successfully and then the VAD build threw (e.g. a good recognizer load followed by a truncated silero_vad.onnx), the already-built recognizer/routed handle was never freed -- isRunning was still false at that point, so stop()/dispose() had nothing to tear down and the handle leaked. Both call sites now wrap _buildNativeState in try/catch and await _teardownNativeState() before rethrowing.
2. setVadSensitivity() called while start() was still loading (_starting true, isRunning/isDebugStreaming both still false) took the "no session" branch: it wrote _vadSensitivity immediately as if applied, but start()'s own in-flight _buildNativeState call would then overwrite that field with whatever sensitivity IT was given, once it finished -- silently discarding the caller's request. setVadSensitivity now treats _starting like a running session: it queues the target into _pendingVadSensitivity instead, and a new _applyPendingVadSensitivityIfAny helper (called from start()/_runDebugWavStream() right after a successful _buildNativeState) picks it up and kicks the existing rebuild-and-swap machinery once native state -- including _vadModelPath -- actually exists.
3. A setVadSensitivity() rebuild's buildVadOffIsolate await can outlive a stop() followed immediately by a new start(): by the time it resolves, _pendingVadSensitivity is null and isRunning is true again (for the NEW session), so the old checks treated it as still valid and installed a VAD built against the OLD session's model path into the new one, freeing the new session's own freshly built VAD in the process. Added a monotonically increasing _sessionGeneration counter, bumped in both _buildNativeState and _teardownNativeState; _rebuildVadUntilCaughtUp now captures the generation right before its await and compares it against the current one once the build resolves (isVadBuildStale, in vad_sensitivity.dart) -- a mismatch means the native state this build was for has moved on, so it's freed instead of installed, the same as the existing "superseded by a newer request" case.
isVadBuildStale is a pure equality check, so it's unit-testable without the native VAD itself, same as shouldSwapVadNow.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* test: cover the native-state-leak, queued-setVadSensitivity, and stale-build fixes
isVadBuildStale gets full pure-function coverage in vad_sensitivity_test.dart (unchanged/advanced-once/advanced-twice/zero-generation cases), the same way shouldSwapVadNow already was.
live_transcriber_config_test.dart gains three groups exercising the parts of the fix reachable without real model files/FFI:
- "start failure cleanup": a start() against a nonexistent model directory throws and leaves isRunning false, and can be retried afterward (the _starting guard resets even when _buildNativeState throws). This exercises the same try/catch/teardown path the leak fix added, though a nonexistent directory fails before the recognizer is ever built, so it can't reach the exact "recognizer built, VAD failed" partial-build point that needs real model files to test directly. - "setVadSensitivity during start()": a call made in the deterministic window between start()'s first `await` and its failure doesn't throw and doesn't build anything of its own -- Dart's async-function semantics (a call runs synchronously up to its first await before yielding) make this window reachable without timing-based flakiness.
The exact-replacement race (fix 3) and the "recognizer built, VAD failed" partial leak (fix 1) stay unverified beyond code review and `flutter analyze` -- both need a real, partially-failing native build to observe, which is the same FFI limitation already documented on LiveTranscriber itself.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* remote: sync RemoteEvent with the new wire fields/event types
The remote path had fallen out of sync with the wire additions the on-device path and desktop subtitle_server.py landed for issue #29: RemoteFinalEvent never parsed audio_s/switched, RemoteRefineEvent never parsed latency_ms (only RemoteFinalEvent did) or audio_s, and model_load/session_reset frames from a desktop server fell through to RemoteUnknownEvent even though ModelLoadSubtitleEvent/ SessionResetSubtitleEvent already exist on the on-device side.
RemoteFinalEvent gains audioSeconds/switched (parsed from audio_s/ switched); RemoteRefineEvent gains latencyMs and audioSeconds. Added RemoteModelLoadEvent and RemoteSessionResetEvent, parsed the same as their on-device ModelLoadEvent/SubtitleEvent counterparts. All four are mapped in HayamimiRemote._onRawEvent onto the matching SubtitleEvent (ModelLoadSubtitleEvent/SessionResetSubtitleEvent for the two new types), so HayamimiRemote.events now carries the same event types the README's "Events" table promises regardless of which path produced them.
subtitle_server.py also emits model_fallback/warning/session_summary/ recluster, which this package still has no typed RemoteEvent for -- left falling back to RemoteUnknownEvent (parseRemoteEvent's default case already does this for anything unrecognized), documented via a doc comment on parseRemoteEvent and a parser test asserting all four degrade that way rather than throwing.
mobile/lib/remote/remote_page.dart's switch on RemoteEvent was exhaustive and needed the two new cases added (both currently no-ops, same as the existing protocol-only frames it already ignores) to keep compiling.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* test: cover the synced RemoteEvent fields/types and their SubtitleEvent mapping
remote_event_test.dart: audio_s/switched on a parsed final event (present and defaulted), latency_ms/audio_s on a parsed refine event (present and defaulted), model_load (both start and done-with-ms), and session_reset. Also asserts model_fallback/warning/session_summary/ recluster all fall back to RemoteUnknownEvent rather than throwing.
New hayamimi_remote_events_test.dart, mirroring hayamimi_live_events_test.dart's fake-transcriber pattern (_FakeRemoteTranscriber extends RemoteTranscriber, events stream injectable): confirms HayamimiRemote._onRawEvent carries audioSeconds/ switched onto FinalSubtitleEvent, latencyMs/audioSeconds onto RefineSubtitleEvent, RemoteModelLoadEvent onto ModelLoadSubtitleEvent, RemoteSessionResetEvent onto SessionResetSubtitleEvent, and that a RemoteUnknownEvent stays dropped from events (not surfaced as a SubtitleEvent).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* test: cover SubtitleBroadcastServer's bindAddress/allowOrigin
Added in a prior commit but shipped without direct test coverage. Three cases: a server given bindAddress: InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4 is reachable on 127.0.0.1, /events sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * by default, and /events sends a custom Access-Control-Allow-Origin when allowOrigin is configured. Headers are read from request.close()'s resolved HttpClientResponse (its future completes once headers arrive, before the SSE body, which never closes on its own) so these don't need to drain or wait out the streaming response.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* docs: document the remote-path event sync and note the review-round fixes
README "Events" section: a paragraph noting HayamimiRemote's RemoteEvent parser understands the same seven wire types (same field names) as the on-device path, plus which four desktop event types (model_fallback/warning/session_summary/recluster) still fall back to RemoteUnknownEvent since this package has no typed RemoteEvent for them yet.
CHANGELOG.md: entries for the RemoteEvent sync and the three LiveTranscriber native-state bugs fixed in this review round (partial native-state leak on a failed build, setVadSensitivity silently losing its effect when called during start(), and a stale VAD rebuild racing a stop()+start() cycle).

entry.title: Embedding (#29, Python): always-on EventHub, runtime setters, /config…
entry.content:
Embedding (#29, Python): always-on EventHub, runtime setters, /config and /reset, session reset (#41)

* engine: runtime setters, structured event hook, speaker reset

Issue #29 asks for hayamimi to be embeddable: an app hosting the engine
needs to change session config without restarting it, and needs to learn
about model-load/fallback/warning conditions structurally instead of by
scraping stderr. RoutedASR previously only accepted forced_lang,
dual_confirm, punctuate, lid_switch_confirm and min_switch_s at
construction time, and its degraded-model notices (missing tier,
unencodable hotwords, missing segmentation VAD, missing second-opinion
model) were print-only.

Adds RoutedASR.set_forced_lang/set_dual_confirm/set_punctuate/
set_lid_switch_confirm/set_min_switch_s, each validating its input and
documented as GIL-safe plain attribute writes (transcribe() runs on a
single decode thread; a setter can be called from any other thread
without a lock). set_forced_lang validates against the new
ROUTABLE_LANGS constant (the tiers the engine actually routes to by
name, as opposed to the omni catch-all) and resets sticky/pending LID
state either way, since a stale switch-confirmation candidate from one
regime must not leak into the other.

Adds an optional on_event callback to RoutedASR.__init__, called for
model_load (start/done, timed) around every real recognizer/LID/punct
build, model_fallback when _get_with_fallback() actually substitutes a
different tier (reported once per requested name per session, matching
the existing stderr print's cardinality so a whole missing tier doesn't
flood an embedder with one event per segment), and warning for the four
degraded-model cases the console already prints for
(hotwords_unencodable, segmentation_vad_unavailable,
second_opinion_unavailable). Every existing print is left in place
unchanged; the callback is purely additive and a no-op when omitted, so
every existing caller (eval scripts, tests) keeps working with no
behavior change.

SpeakerLabeler.reset() forgets all centroids/counts/aliases/merge
history/confirmation state without rebuilding the CAM++ embedding
extractor, so a live session can restart its speaker identity from
scratch without paying a model reload.

scripts/realtime_transcribe.py and scripts/subtitle_server.py are not
wired to any of this yet (next commits); tests/test_second_opinion.py's
_FakeASR stub gained a no-op _emit() to match RoutedASR's new call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* server: split EventHub out of SubtitleServer, add /config and /reset

Issue #29's structured-event requirement needs a pub/sub hub that exists
whether or not --serve's HTTP server does, since an app embedding the
engine directly (no HTTP layer at all) still wants model_load/warning/
session_summary events. SubtitleServer previously WAS the pub/sub core
(clients list, refine replay buffer, lock), so there was nowhere to
publish an event without an HTTP server running.

Pulls that core into a new EventHub class: publish()/subscribe()/
unsubscribe() unchanged in behavior (including the refine-replay-to-new-
subscribers list), plus add_listener() for an in-process callback that
doesn't need JSON round-tripping. A listener that raises is reported to
stderr once per callback (not once per event) and then stays swallowed,
so one broken listener can't spam the console for the rest of the
session, matching the same "never let an event-hub problem break the
pipeline" principle asr_engine.RoutedASR._emit() (previous commit) applies
on the publisher side. final()'s convenience method gains the audio_s/
lid_ms/decode_ms/switched fields realtime_transcribe.py's drain_segments()
will start passing next.

SubtitleServer now wraps an EventHub (auto-created if none is passed,
so existing standalone construction still works) and becomes a thin
HTTP/SSE front over it -- every previously-public method (publish/
partial/final/subscribe/unsubscribe/start, the /replacements and
/itn_overrides endpoints) is unchanged, so scripts/ws_ingest.py's
`self.subtitle_server.subscribe()`/`.unsubscribe()` calls needed no edit.

Adds a RuntimeControls container (asr/translator_pool/live_vad/reset_fn
handles, all optional) backing three new endpoints: GET /config reads
the live session's forced language, dual-confirm, punctuation,
LID-switch-confirm, min-switch-guard, translation targets and VAD
sensitivity; POST /config applies any subset of those (400 with the
setter's own message on an invalid value); POST /reset runs a caller-
supplied session-reset closure. All three 404 when no controls are
attached, matching the existing /replacements pattern. subtitle_server.py
still only imports stdlib, so RuntimeControls reads its handles by duck
typing rather than importing realtime_transcribe.py's classes.

Nothing constructs an EventHub/RuntimeControls from realtime_transcribe.py
yet (next commit); this file's own behavior for existing callers
(ws_ingest.py, the OBS overlay, the dashboard) is unchanged, confirmed via
tests/test_overlay_parity.py and tests/test_ws_ingest.py.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* pipeline: always-on EventHub, LiveVad, TranslatorPool, session reset

Wires the previous two commits' pieces (RoutedASR.on_event, EventHub,
RuntimeControls) into realtime_transcribe.py's actual pipeline and adds
the remaining GitHub issue #29 pieces: runtime VAD sensitivity, shared
translation targets, and a full session reset that doesn't rebuild any
loaded model.

main() now always constructs an EventHub before building the engine
(RoutedASR(..., on_event=hub.publish)) and passes it to PartialPrinter/
Refiner/TranslationWorker; --serve only adds an HTTP/SSE front over the
SAME hub instead of gating whether events exist at all. Every
`if server is not None` around an event publish is gone -- drain_
segments(), Refiner's two refine-event sites, and TranslationWorker now
publish unconditionally. drain_segments()'s `final` event gained
audio_s/lid_ms/decode_ms/switched (switched tracked via a new
SessionStats.last_final_lang, since asr.last_lang has already advanced
past the value needed for the comparison by the time drain_segments()
reads the result). Refine events gained audio_s. A caught diarization
failure in Refiner._emit_turns() now also publishes a `warning` event
(diarization_failed) alongside its existing stderr print.

Adds LiveVad, wrapping the sherpa-onnx VAD so --min-silence/--max-speech/
threshold can change at runtime: sherpa-onnx has no in-place setters, so
a set_sensitivity() request is deferred and only rebuilds the detector at
the next chunk boundary where it isn't mid-segment (rebuilding mid-speech
would drop that segment's audio and reset the endpointer mid-word).
Implements the subset of the sherpa VAD API run_stream()/drain_segments()
use, so it's a drop-in for build_vad() at every existing call site;
build_vad() itself is untouched for the eval scripts that call it
directly.

Adds TranslatorPool, a shared mutable set of ja->target translators used
by both TranslationWorker (live) and Refiner (second pass) so a runtime
add/remove target (POST /config's "translate" key) applies to both at
once. build_translators() now populates a pool instead of returning a
plain dict; an unsupported --translate code still just prints a stderr
note and continues (existing CLI behavior), while TranslatorPool.
add_target() itself raises ValueError so the HTTP path gets a clean 400.
main() now always constructs the pool and its TranslationWorker, even
with no --translate targets at startup, specifically so a target added
later at runtime has a live worker already pulling ja finals to
translate -- an empty pool costs nothing (the worker iterates zero
targets per line).

Adds SessionStats.reset(), AudioHistory.clear(), Refiner.reset() (drops
pending spans/group state, clears history, writes a visible separator
into an open transcript file, and waits for the refine worker queue to
drain first so it can't race an in-flight task), and the module-level
reset_live_session(asr, refiner, labeler, stats, hub, live_vad=None)
orchestrator: flush pending refine -> publish session_summary (so it
describes the ending session, not the zeroed one) -> reset each piece ->
asr.reset_session() -> publish session_reset. live_vad is accepted for
signature symmetry but deliberately untouched -- VAD sensitivity is
orthogonal to a conversation's identity, not part of what a session reset
should change. main()'s own shutdown block publishes the same
session_summary shape via a new shared _session_summary_event() helper,
and wires a RuntimeControls instance onto the SubtitleServer (when
--serve) whose reset_fn closes over reset_live_session().

Verified against the real model catalog (not just tests/): `--wav
testdata/multi_sentence_ja.wav --no-realtime --no-refine` reproduces the
exact prior console output, and a `--input ws --serve` run answered GET/
POST /config (including a 400 on an unsupported --lang code) and POST
/reset correctly, with model_load/session_start/session_summary/
session_reset events observed on /events in that order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: cover EventHub, runtime setters, TranslatorPool, LiveVad, resets

Adds tests/test_embed_runtime.py, 45 tests for GitHub issue #29's new
surface: EventHub publish/subscribe/refine-replay/add_listener (including
that a listener's exception is reported once per callback, not once per
event -- publishes twice through a raising listener and checks stderr
only got one report); drain_segments()'s `final` event carries audio_s/
lid_ms/decode_ms and the `switched` field is false on the session's first
final, true on a language change, false on a repeat, and resets cleanly
through SessionStats.reset(); TranslationWorker publishing on a bare
EventHub with no SubtitleServer/HTTP server at all, and being a silent
no-op with an empty TranslatorPool (main()'s always-on wiring); RoutedASR's
five setters validating and taking effect, gated behind a needs_lid_model
skip since __init__ still builds the real LID model eagerly; TranslatorPool
add/remove/idempotence with translator construction stubbed via
monkeypatching the module-level _build_translator function; LiveVad
deferring a sensitivity change while a stubbed VAD reports mid-speech and
applying it at the next safe chunk boundary; SpeakerLabeler.reset(),
AudioHistory.clear(), and Refiner.reset() (including that reset() writes
its separator into a transcript file that stays open, not reopened);
reset_live_session()'s five-step ordering, particularly that a still-
pending refine group is flushed and reflected in the session_summary
event's refine_groups_closed count BEFORE stats.reset() zeroes it back
out; and SubtitleServer's GET/POST /config and POST /reset over a real
http.client connection against a server started on port 0, including the
404-without-controls and 400-on-invalid-value cases.

Whole suite: 263 passed, 4 skipped (up from the 218 passed, 4 skipped
baseline -- the 4 skips are pre-existing and unrelated to this change;
none of the new tests skip in this environment, since models/ is a
junction to the real model catalog here).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: document runtime control and structured events (issue #29)

An app embedding this engine could only set session config once, at
construction, and had no reliable way to learn about a model load
failing or a fallback kicking in short of scraping stderr and the
console's free-text diagnostic line -- structured events only existed
behind --serve at all. The last few commits fixed both (an always-on
EventHub, RoutedASR runtime setters, TranslatorPool, LiveVad, session
reset); this documents them.

Adds "Embedding: runtime control and structured events" to both READMEs,
right after the existing "Embedding in another app" section: the
add_listener()/subscribe() consumption paths, a reference table of every
event type's JSON shape and when it fires, and the three --serve-only
HTTP endpoints (GET/POST /config, POST /reset) with curl examples,
including the one non-obvious behavior worth calling out explicitly --
a VAD sensitivity change can't apply immediately (sherpa-onnx has no
in-place setter) and is deferred to the next point the detector isn't
mid-utterance. Also adds one row to each README's Features table
pointing at the new section.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: thread-safe session reset, VAD input validation, pool locking

Review round 1 on this branch found three real bugs, all in the runtime
control surface added over the previous five commits.

1. POST /reset ran reset_live_session() directly on the HTTP handler
   thread while run_stream()'s decode thread could be concurrently inside
   drain_segments() (SpeakerLabeler.match_embedding(), Refiner.add_span(),
   stats.latencies_ms.append()) or Refiner.maybe_refine(). SpeakerLabeler.
   reset() clearing _centroids/_counts mid-match_embedding() could raise
   IndexError there, and two threads both calling maybe_refine() race on
   Refiner.spans with nothing serializing them. Fixed the same way
   LiveVad already defers a VAD rebuild: a new ControlQueue class queues
   a callable and hands back a threading.Event, and run_stream() calls
   control.poll() once per chunk (right alongside its existing stop_event
   check) to actually run whatever's queued, on the decode thread.
   RuntimeControls.reset_fn now submits reset_live_session(...) to the
   queue and waits on the Event with a 10s timeout (RESET_TIMEOUT_S);
   POST /reset answers 200 once it actually ran, or 202 {"ok": false,
   "pending": true} if the timeout elapses first (e.g. --input ws with no
   client currently sending audio, since nothing reaches a chunk boundary
   to poll from). reset_live_session()'s docstring now documents that
   calling it directly is only safe from the thread already driving
   run_stream(), or via a ControlQueue that thread is polling.

2. LiveVad.set_sensitivity() stored whatever it was given and only
   reached build_vad() with it later, on the decode thread, when
   _maybe_apply_pending() next ran -- so POST /config {"vad":
   {"threshold": "abc"}} (or a negative/zero/out-of-range number) would
   crash the decode loop instead of returning 400. Validation now happens
   synchronously inside set_sensitivity() itself, before anything is
   queued into self._pending: type-checked (int/float, with bool
   explicitly excluded since it's a subclass of int in Python) and
   range-checked (0 < threshold <= 1, min_silence > 0, max_speech > 0),
   raising ValueError with the offending key's name. An explicit None
   (including JSON null from a partial POST /config body, which can't be
   told apart from an absent key) still means "no change" and is never
   validated, matching the existing "no change" contract.

3. TranslatorPool.items()/targets read self._order/self._translators
   without the lock add_target()/remove_target() hold, so a remove_target()
   landing mid-iteration could KeyError inside the live TranslationWorker's
   daemon thread -- which has no try/except around its loop, so that
   silently killed translation for the rest of the session. Both methods
   now snapshot fully under self._lock; the returned (lang, translator)
   pairs hold real object references, so a target removed a moment AFTER
   the snapshot is harmless (at most one extra translation using an
   object the caller already holds, never a stale re-lookup by name).
